To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the prenyl group is a common modification of proteins, 2) it is a reversible modification, 3) the farnesyl group is attached to the carboxyl terminus of a CaaX motif, and 4) the carboxyl group is a methyl ester.
the prenylation of RAS proteins is essential for their function, and that the carboxyl‐methylation of the prenylated cysteine is essential for the prenylated RAS proteins to function.

the addition of a single amino acid, lysine, to the end of a protein sequence can dramatically increase the stability of the protein, and that the addition of this amino acid is mediated by a protein‐protein interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of new biologically active molecules and the development of new synthetic methods.
the synthesis of novel and biologically active compounds, and the development of new synthetic methodologies.
the development of new and efficient methods for the synthesis of biologically active compounds, and the application of this technology to the study of molecular biology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the farnesyl group is essential for the function of Ras, but that the geranyl group is not.
the prenylation of proteins in mammalian cells is catalyzed by the enzyme geranylgeranyltransferase type I.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the prenyl group is attached to the C‐terminus of a protein by the action of farnesyltransferase and the carboxy‐methyl group is attached to a specific lysine residue by the action of a methyltransferase.
we have found the use of radiolabeled mevanolone and [3H‐ methyl]methionine to be very useful tools for identifying proteins modified by prenylation and methylation.
we have developed methods for labeling proteins in cells with prenyl groups and with methyl groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prenylation of proteins can be used as an important tool in the investigation of protein function.
prenylation of proteins in the plasma membrane is not a static process.
the prenyl group is not a static appendage, but is a dynamic entity.
